cloud_security_and_permissions_policy.heading: Collaborate Without Accidentally Sharing Sensitive Information
principles: Least-Privilege Access: Grant Viewer or Commenter access by default; reserve Editor for active co-authors.
Permission Inheritance: Understand that child files inherit folder access; broadly shared folders cannot be partially locked down from within.
Restricted Confidential Folders: Keep sensitive financial, HR, or client records in dedicated restricted locations rather than general team drives.
Owner Privacy: Recognize that sharing links and files exposes the owner's account identity to viewers; use supervised test environments in training.
Version History Auditing: Track collaborator revisions, inspect timestamps, and restore earlier clean drafts when unwanted modifications occur.

forms_and_linked_sheets_policy.heading: Collect Information Once. Organize It Responsibly.
principles: Independent Permission Audits: Google Forms collaborators do not automatically share the same access rules as the linked response Sheet; both must be audited independently.
Synthetic Classroom Datasets: Real client PII, government IDs, student personal details, or financial accounts must never be collected or stored in practice forms.
Data Minimization: Request only the fields strictly required for the business process; use validation rules to ensure data integrity.
Downstream Refresh Awareness: Linked Sheets accept new submissions automatically, but downstream reports, pivot summaries, and dashboard slides require deliberate configuration or manual refresh.

responsible_gemini_ai_policy.heading: Use Gemini to Assist Work. Keep Humans Responsible for Decisions.
principles: AI as Assistant: Use Gemini for drafting emails, outlining slide decks, summarizing reports, and explaining formulas, never as the unverified source of truth.
Mandatory Factual Verification: Cross-check every date, stakeholder name, numeric calculation, and contractual deadline against verified source documents.
Free-Account Fallback: Certification exercises never require a paid Gemini tier; instructors provide synthetic AI sample outputs for manual review where accounts lack AI licenses.
Data Confidentiality: Prohibit pasting non-public enterprise information or client details into public or consumer AI prompts.

meeting_and_communication_standards.heading: Professional Connected Communication Standard
principles: Asynchronous Precision: Write structured emails with explicit subjects, numbered action items, clear assignees, and stated deadlines.
Timezone Diligence: Verify multi-region attendees in Google Calendar before issuing invitations; configure working hours and buffer times.
Meet Professional Etiquette: Arrive with prepared Docs agendas, designate a scribe for follow-up documentation, and establish explicit consent before initiating any recorded session.
Paid Feature Transparency: Acknowledge that recording, automated transcription, and AI meeting summaries are tier-dependent and not universal across free accounts.

tools_and_licensing_boundary.heading: Core Accessible Tools vs. Paid Workspace Features
principles: Core Tools Covered: All foundational skills utilize Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Calendar, Meet, and Forms available across personal and standard Google accounts.
No Admin Console Requirement: Enterprise domain provisioning, DNS record mapping, Google Vault, and DLP rules are excluded from this operational certification.
Shared Drives Awareness: Organization-managed shared storage is taught conceptually; individual lab work operates safely within My Drive hierarchies.
Introductory Apps Script: Script triggers and macros are presented as awareness concepts; no JavaScript or Apps Script programming is required to earn certification.

curriculum.title: Cloud Workplace & Security
curriculum.objective: Understand Google Workspace fundamentals, organize cloud information and use appropriate file-access and security practices.
lessons: 1.1 Cloud Productivity Fundamentals: Cloud applications; Browser-based work; File synchronization; Team collaboration; Connected workflows.
1.2 Consumer Google vs Google Workspace: Personal Google account; Organization-managed Workspace account; Account ownership; Subscription differences; Administrative policies.
1.3 Workspace Application Ecosystem: Gmail; Drive; Docs; Sheets; Slides; Calendar; Meet; Forms; Tasks; Gemini awareness.
1.4 Google Account Security: Password practices; Two-step verification; Account recovery awareness; Device security; Phishing prevention.
1.5 Google Drive Navigation: My Drive; Files; Folders; Search; Starred; Shortcuts; Recent files interface.
1.6 Folder Architecture: Project folders; Department folders; Shared resources; Archive systems; Naming conventions.
1.7 File Organization: Document naming; Version designations; Date conventions; Ownership structure; Folder purpose definition.
1.8 File Uploads & Conversions: Uploading local files; Office-to-Docs conversion where appropriate; File preview; Direct opening; Safe download protocols.
1.9 Google File Types: Native Docs, Sheets, Slides, Forms; Handling uploaded Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and PDF files.
1.10 Sharing Fundamentals: Restricted access; Adding specific people; General link sharing; Recognizing primary file ownership.
1.11 Permission Roles: Viewer permissions; Commenter permissions; Editor permissions; Owner roles and delegation.
1.12 Least-Privilege Access: Granting minimum necessary permissions; Avoiding widespread editor access; Periodic external sharing audits.
1.13 Inherited Permissions: Folder-level sharing dynamics; Child file access inheritance; Effective permissions; Limits on restricting a file inside a broadly shared folder.
1.14 Restricted Folders: Isolating sensitive departmental materials; Limiting subfolder visibility where supported; Preventing confidential leaks.
1.15 Shared Drives Awareness: Organization-managed shared drives; Team-owned storage vs personal My Drive; Subscription and admin requirements.
1.16 File Ownership Management: Creator vs owner; Collaborator rights; Ownership transfer protocols and organizational restrictions.
1.17 Version History & Recovery: Tracking revisions; Identifying collaborator edits; Restoring earlier clean versions; Creating named milestone versions.
1.18 File Recovery & Trash Governance: Google Drive Trash lifecycle; Restoring deleted files; Recovery limitations; Ownership deletion impact.
1.19 Offline Access Awareness: Enabling Google Docs offline mode; System setup requirements; Synchronization risks on shared devices; Data safety.
1.20 Security Risks & Best Practices: Mitigating public link leaks; Preventing accidental external editors; Avoiding unnecessary downloads; Protecting sensitive spreadsheets.
curriculum.hands_on_lab: Create an office folder structure using fictional business information featuring main workspace, project, documents, reports, meetings, forms, and deliverables folders. Demonstrate restricted files, viewer, commenter, editor access, version history, and a permissions audit.
curriculum.deliverable: Google Drive Office Workspace & Permission Matrix
curriculum.security_considerations: Use only synthetic business information. Never make all files public for convenience; enforce strict least-privilege role assignment.

curriculum.title: Gmail, Calendar & Meet
curriculum.objective: Manage professional email, scheduling, meetings and follow-up workflows efficiently and accurately.
lessons: 2.1 Gmail Professional Communication: Inbox organization; Compose; Reply; Reply All discipline; Forwarding; Business signatures.
2.2 Professional Email Structure: Clear subject lines; Professional greetings; Structured body copy; Explicit call-to-action; Standard sign-offs.
2.3 Recipient Management: Appropriate use of To, CC, and BCC; Preserving client privacy; Avoiding accidental company-wide replies.
2.4 Attachments & Drive Sharing: Direct attachments vs Google Drive links; Automatic permission verification before sending; File-size limits.
2.5 Gmail Labels: Creating hierarchical labels; Color-coding projects; Differentiating internal vs client conversations.
2.6 Gmail Filters & Automation: Automating inbox triage based on sender, subject, and keywords; Applying labels; Archiving and skipping inbox.
2.7 Advanced Gmail Search: Search operators (from:, to:, subject:, has:attachment, filename:, after:, before:); Finding lost communications.
2.8 Stars, Priority & Snooze: Multi-star systems for triage; Snoozing emails for future review; Zero-inbox workflow principles.
2.9 Email Templates: Creating and inserting reusable email drafts; Interface and account requirements for template activation.
2.10 Business Email Quality Assurance: Verifying email objectives; Proofreading recipient addresses; Checking attached links; Professional tone.
2.11 Calendar Fundamentals: Navigating Day, Week, Month, and Schedule views; Creating and categorizing personal and team events.
2.12 Event Scheduling Discipline: Informative event titles; Descriptive meeting briefs; Timezone validation; Setting appropriate notification buffers.
2.13 Calendar Invitations & RSVP: Inviting internal and external guests; Tracking RSVP statuses (Yes, Maybe, No); Managing updates and cancellations.
2.14 Multi-Timezone Coordination: Managing time differences across India and global zones; Secondary timezone display; Preventing scheduling conflicts.
2.15 Recurring Meetings & Exceptions: Setting up daily standups, weekly reviews, and monthly townhalls; Modifying single occurrences vs series.
2.16 Shared Calendars Awareness: Viewing team availability; Creating secondary departmental calendars; Calendar visibility settings.
2.17 Google Meet Fundamentals: Joining sessions via link, Calendar, or phone; Microphone and camera settings; Meeting chat; Screen sharing controls.
2.18 Meeting Roles & Controls: Meeting organizer; Host management tools; Co-host delegation where supported; Participant management and muting.
2.19 Meeting Agendas in Practice: Drafting clear objectives, discussion topics, time allocations, and expected decision outcomes in Docs.
2.20 Virtual Meeting Etiquette: Punctuality, background audio hygiene, camera conventions, screen presentation protocols, and consent standards.
2.21 Meeting Follow-Up Documentation: Capturing decisions, assigning action items with explicit owners and deadlines, and compiling follow-up notes.
2.22 Meet Recording Awareness: Workspace plan eligibility; Host permissions; Recording storage in Drive; Mandatory participant notification and consent.
2.23 Meeting Transcription & AI Notes: Plan requirements for automated transcriptions; Supported language limits; AI summary review and correction.
2.24 Integrated Communication Workflow: Connecting email invitations, Calendar events, Meet links, shared Docs agendas, and Sheets tracking.
curriculum.hands_on_lab: Prepare a complete fictional team meeting workflow: draft an invitation email, schedule a Calendar event with Meet details, prepare an agenda in Docs, allocate action items, write a follow-up email, and record decisions in a tracker.
curriculum.security_considerations: Perform labs using supervised practice accounts; never send unsolicited invitations to external third parties; respect meeting consent guidelines.

curriculum.title: Docs, Sheets & Slides
curriculum.objective: Create and maintain professional collaborative documents, spreadsheets and presentations.
lessons: 3.1 Connected Office Documents: Interoperability between text, data, and slides; Shared cloud file ownership; Universal version tracking.
3.2 Google Docs Interface: Modern Docs navigation; Document outline; Page setup; Word count; Full-screen and pageless views.
3.3 Professional Document Structure: Title hierarchy; Headings (H1, H2, H3); Body typography; Bulleted lists; Tables; Visual breaks.
3.4 Styles & Formatting Consistency: Applying and updating default styles; Document styling templates; Enhancing readability and scanability.
3.5 Real-Time Docs Collaboration: Co-authoring etiquette; Commenting (@mentioning team members); Suggesting mode; Accepting and rejecting edits.
3.6 Document Version History: Reviewing historical revisions; Naming significant milestone versions; Comparing edits across collaborators.
3.7 Document Sharing Protocols: Managing Viewer, Commenter, and Editor access; Preventing unauthorized download, copy, or print on sensitive files.
3.8 Smart Chips in Docs: Embedding interactive chips for people, files, dates, calendar events, and dropdown status trackers.
3.9 Google Sheets Fundamentals: Grid architecture; Rows, columns, cells, and ranges; Data formats (numbers, currency, dates, text).
3.10 Business Formulas in Practice: Essential office formulas (SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, COUNTA, COUNTIF, SUMIF, basic IF logic, and TODAY).
3.11 Team Task & Operations Tracker: Designing structured trackers with Task ID, Description, Assignee, Priority, Status, Due Date, and Notes.
3.12 Data Validation Controls: Configuring dropdown menus for status fields; Preventing invalid text entries; Enforcing clean team inputs.
3.13 Conditional Formatting: Highlighting overdue deadlines; Flagging high-priority issues; Visualizing project completion percentages.
3.14 Sorting, Filters & Filter Views: Quick sorting; Multi-column filtering; Creating collaborative Filter Views without altering teammates' views.
3.15 Basic Spreadsheet Reporting: Summary calculation cards; Category counts; Status distribution charts; Clear labeling and headers.
3.16 Collaborative Editing in Sheets: Concurrent editing rules; Cell commenting; Protecting specific ranges and sheets to avoid accidental overwrites.
3.17 Google Slides Fundamentals: Setting up presentation decks; Applying theme masters; Working with layouts, text boxes, and shapes.
3.18 Shared Presentations: Multi-user deck collaboration; Slide-level commenting; Assigning slide review tasks; Presentation approvals.
3.19 Business Slide Design Quality: Contrast and typography standards; Avoiding crowded text; Creating structured 3-part layout cards.
3.20 Linking Spreadsheet Information: Importing charts and tables from Sheets into Slides; Linked vs unlinked insertion modes.
3.21 Linked-Data Limitations: Understanding update and refresh mechanics; Handling broken links; Permission requirements for linked source sheets.
3.22 Cloud Version Control: Reconciling divergent versions; Archiving old presentations; Ensuring single source of truth across team assets.
3.23 Exporting & File Conversion: Exporting Docs to PDF; Exporting Sheets to CSV/PDF; Converting Slides to PPTX/PDF; Preserving fidelity.
3.24 Document Accessibility Fundamentals: Using true headings for screen readers; Providing alternative text for images; Ensuring WCAG contrast.
curriculum.hands_on_lab: Build a collaborative team project package: 1 professional Google Doc with styles and comments, 1 Google Sheets tracker with data validation and formulas, 1 Google Slides update presentation with linked chart, and version history evidence.
curriculum.deliverable: Google Docs + Sheets + Slides Team Collaboration Pack
curriculum.security_considerations: Maintain strict boundary: does not replace advanced Excel data modeling or Word desktop publishing. Use clean, non-confidential operational data.

curriculum.title: Forms & Team Workflows
curriculum.objective: Use Forms, Sheets, Drive and appropriate task-coordination practices to manage recurring office workflows.
lessons: 4.1 Digital Office Workflow Concepts: Inputs, validation, processing, team review, reporting outputs, and clear process ownership.
4.2 Google Forms Fundamentals: Form creation; Title, description, sections; Header branding; Organizing question flow logically.
4.3 Question Types & Validation: Short answer, paragraph, multiple choice, checkboxes, dropdown, linear scale, date, and input validation rules.
4.4 Form Design & UX: Writing unambiguous questions; Grouping related items into sections; Avoiding unnecessary data collection.
4.5 Required Fields & Branching: Setting mandatory fields; Section navigation based on user answers; Ensuring clean submission pathways.
4.6 Form Settings Management: Email collection controls; Limiting to 1 response; Enabling response editing; Confirmation messages.
4.7 Form Access & Permissions: Collaborator editing access vs respondent submission access; Differentiating editor rights from respondent rights.
4.8 Publishing & Controlled Distribution: Generating short URLs; Embedding in internal docs; Restricted organizational sharing vs public access.
4.9 Analyzing Form Responses: Viewing aggregate summaries, question breakdowns, and individual response submissions in Google Forms.
4.10 Linking Forms to Google Sheets: Creating a new response spreadsheet; Linking to an existing destination sheet; Managing incoming timestamps.
4.11 Response Sheet Permissions Governance: Independent security: why removing a Form collaborator does NOT revoke access to the linked Sheet.
4.12 Data Quality & Sanitization: Handling duplicate submissions; Standardizing text inputs; Validating date formatting in the response sheet.
4.13 Workflow Case 1 — Internal Service Request: Request submission via Form; Automatic row logging; Triage assignment; Status tracking in Sheets.
4.14 Workflow Case 2 — Office Feedback Survey: Anonymous feedback collection; Aggregating satisfaction metrics; Presenting chart summaries in Slides.
4.15 Google Tasks Coordination: Creating personal and shared task lists; Assigning due dates; Integrating Tasks within Gmail and Google Calendar.
4.16 Team Operations Coordination: Establishing task owners, priorities, progress milestones, and scheduled weekly review checkpoints.
4.17 Drive Folder Architecture for Workflows: Organizing form drafts, raw response datasets, cleaned reporting sheets, and executive presentations.
4.18 Access Governance Auditing: Restricting access to raw survey response data; Applying principle of least privilege across operational pipelines.
4.19 Shared Drives in Team Workflows: Understanding organizational file ownership; Member permissions (Manager, Content Manager, Contributor, Viewer).
4.20 Version Control for Operational Workflows: Documenting changes to form questions; Managing revision notes in response trackers.
4.21 Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) Documentation: Writing clear step-by-step documentation for form management, data review, and handoff.
4.22 Human Approval & Sign-Offs: Structuring human checkpoints in office workflows; Avoiding claims of unverified total automation.
4.23 Google Apps Script Awareness: Architectural overview of Apps Script; Concept of triggers (onEdit, onFormSubmit); Security permissions and risks.
4.24 Privacy, Compliance & Data Ethics: Minimizing personal data collection; Storing consent records; Establishing retention and deletion schedules.
curriculum.hands_on_lab: Design and deploy an internal-office request workflow: create a Google Form, collect synthetic submissions, route data to a linked Google Sheet, build an operational tracking view with validation and status tags, and audit permissions.
curriculum.security_considerations: Crucial rule: Verify both Form and linked Sheet permissions independently. Never collect real PII, financial details, or government IDs in classroom forms.

curriculum.title: Gemini-Assisted Productivity

lessons: 5.1 Gemini Ecosystem Overview: Gemini standalone app vs embedded Gemini features across Google Workspace applications; Feature boundaries.
5.2 Plan Eligibility & Subscriptions: Free Google accounts vs Google Workspace Business/Enterprise tiers vs Google AI Pro add-ons.
5.3 Free vs Paid Feature Availability: Identifying which AI features are included by plan; Understanding feature rollouts and administrative toggles.
5.4 Gemini in Gmail: Drafting professional emails; Summarizing long email threads; Adjusting tone (formal, concise, elaborate); Human review.
5.5 Gemini in Google Docs: 'Help me write' drafting; Rewriting text for clarity; Summarizing documents; Structuring executive summaries.
5.6 Gemini in Google Sheets: Generating formula suggestions; Explaining complex formula logic; Organizing data categories; Creating starter tables.
5.7 Gemini in Google Slides: Brainstorming presentation outlines; Drafting slide headlines and bullet points; Generating concept imagery.
5.8 Advanced Slides Generation Awareness: Multi-slide generation updates (June 2026); Plan eligibility (Business Standard+, Google AI Pro); Language limits.
5.9 Gemini in Google Drive: Summarizing stored documents and reports; Finding information across authorized files without manual reading.
5.10 Gemini in Google Meet: Automated meeting notes (where licensed); Action item extraction; Consent protocols and participant notification.
5.11 Gemini in Google Forms: Assisted form and survey generation; Drafting relevant question options; Human review of question bias.
5.12 Business Prompting Framework: Structuring prompts with Task, Context, Source Data, Constraints, Desired Output Format, and Verification.
5.13 AI for Business Correspondence: Drafting meeting requests, follow-up notes, vendor responses, and executive announcements safely.
5.14 AI for Document Editing: Checking draft completeness; Formatting unstructured notes into clean tables; Refining tone for external audiences.
5.15 AI for Spreadsheet Interpretation: Deciphering unfamiliar formulas; Verifying mathematical assumptions; Checking calculation boundaries manually.
5.16 AI for Presentation Planning: Generating structured 5-slide deck structures from written briefs; Outlining key takeaways and speaker points.
5.17 Understanding AI Hallucinations: Recognizing invented facts, incorrect dates, fabricated meeting decisions, and erroneous spreadsheet formulas.
5.18 Rigorous Factual Verification: Cross-referencing AI outputs against primary records; Validating figures, names, deadlines, and direct quotes.
5.19 Human Accountability & Approval: The mandatory rule of human sign-off: never sending AI drafts without line-by-line editorial inspection.
5.20 Enterprise Data Privacy & Security: Rules against inputting confidential client records, employee personal data, or proprietary trade secrets.
5.21 Responsible AI Workflow Standard: The 6-step cycle: Draft → Review → Verify → Correct → Approve → Deliver.
5.22 Free-Account Classroom Fallback: Using instructor-provided synthetic AI outputs for evaluation exercises when student accounts lack AI tiers.
5.23 AI as Copilot, Not Replacement: Demonstrating manual proficiency across all core Google apps before applying AI acceleration.
5.24 Feature Rollout & Policy Monitoring: Monitoring Google Workspace updates, regional availability, language support, and institutional controls.
curriculum.hands_on_lab: Perform three supervised AI assistance exercises using synthetic data: improve an email draft, summarize an office report, and explain a formula/outline. Identify and correct deliberate AI hallucinations. Use provided sample outputs if Gemini is unavailable.
curriculum.security_considerations: Gemini is optional and not a paid requirement for certification. Real confidential data must never be pasted into public AI prompts.

curriculum.deliverable: Collaborative Digital Office Workspace — Final Capstone
curriculum.security_considerations: Full verification of least-privilege permissions, zero public link exposure, and complete separation of synthetic practice data from personal accounts.

learning_outcomes: Explain cloud productivity fundamentals, browser-based synchronization, and modern digital office workflows.
Understand the key distinctions between consumer Google accounts and organization-managed Google Workspace plans.
Distinguish free personal Google tools from subscription-dependent enterprise administration and AI features.
Navigate Google Drive confidently, utilizing My Drive, search bars, starred items, shortcuts, and recent views.
Create well-structured, logical folder architectures for projects, departments, shared assets, and archives.
Apply professional, standardized file-naming conventions incorporating dates, versions, and project codes.
Understand Google file ownership rules, creator privileges, and constraints on organizational ownership transfers.
Manage sharing permissions accurately across Viewer, Commenter, and Editor access levels.
Recognize how child files inherit parent folder access and inspect effective permissions to prevent data exposure.
Utilize Google Drive and Docs version history to track edits, inspect collaborator revisions, and restore earlier drafts.
Implement foundational Google account security measures, including strong passwords and two-step verification.
Identify common email phishing risks, suspicious attachments, and spoofed sender addresses.
Compose clear, professional Gmail messages structured with explicit subject lines, greetings, and call-to-actions.
Create and manage Gmail labels and color codes to organize incoming project and client correspondence.
Build automated Gmail filters to label, categorize, prioritize, and archive recurring business emails.
Execute advanced Gmail searches using targeted search operators to locate specific messages and attachments rapidly.
Create and manage Google Calendar events with precise titles, descriptions, buffers, and notification reminders.
Invite internal and external attendees to meetings, monitor RSVP statuses, and handle reschedule notifications cleanly.
Coordinate meetings across regional and international timezones without scheduling misalignments.
Join and facilitate Google Meet sessions, managing audio, video, chat, screen sharing, and participant controls.
Prepare structured meeting agendas in Google Docs with stated objectives, discussion topics, and time limits.
Document meeting outcomes into concise follow-up summaries with explicit action items, assignees, and deadlines.
Create professional documents in Google Docs using standardized heading hierarchies, tables, lists, and formatting.
Collaborate in real-time in Google Docs using comments, @mentions, suggestion mode, and revision resolution.
Review, name, and compare document versions to maintain an authoritative single source of truth.
Build structured team operations trackers and registers in Google Sheets with appropriate data types.
Apply essential business formulas in Google Sheets, including SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, COUNTIF, and IF logic.
Implement data validation rules in Google Sheets to enforce dropdown selections and prevent inaccurate entries.
Apply conditional formatting rules in Google Sheets to highlight overdue deadlines, priorities, and status updates.
Create collaborative presentations in Google Slides with cohesive themes, clean layouts, and visual hierarchy.
Design user-friendly Google Forms with appropriate question types, sections, and input validation rules.
Configure Google Form settings to collect necessary information ethically while respecting respondent privacy.
Link Google Forms to dedicated Google Sheets destinations to automatically capture incoming response records.
Audit Google Forms and linked response Sheet permissions independently to avoid unintended public data exposure.
Organize personal and team action items using Google Tasks connected with Gmail and Calendar schedules.
Apply safe sharing practices, enforcing least-privilege access and eliminating unmonitored public links.
Explain Gemini AI capabilities and limitations across Gmail, Docs, Sheets, and Slides.
Perform rigorous factual verification on all AI-generated content, cross-checking calculations, dates, and names.
Complete an end-to-end connected office workflow linking email, calendar, docs, sheets, slides, and forms.
Audit access permissions across the entire workspace and compile a comprehensive handover documentation package.

portfolio.title: Collaborative Digital Office Workspace
portfolio.objective: Produce one integrated cloud-office collaboration capstone comprising eight operational components that demonstrate how Google Workspace applications work together safely, accurately, and efficiently in everyday business practice.
portfolio.countingRule: One integrated capstone with eight cohesive components demonstrating complete digital office operations.

deliverables.title: Shared Office Workspace
deliverables.scenario: Construct a logically structured Google Drive folder system containing dedicated subfolders for project docs, data trackers, presentations, forms/response files, meetings, and deliverables with consistent naming and verified ownership.
requirements: Hierarchical folder architecture (Projects, Docs, Reports, Meetings, Forms, Deliverables).
Standardized file-naming convention incorporating dates, project initials, and version codes.
Clear ownership documentation distinguishing individual vs team-shared storage.
Implementation of restricted folders separating sensitive operational materials.

deliverables.title: Professional Google Document
deliverables.scenario: Author an executive project operations plan or standard operating procedure in Google Docs utilizing formal heading styles, tables, numbered procedures, and active collaborative review evidence.
requirements: Structured typographic hierarchy (Title, H1, H2, H3, clean paragraph spacing).
Evidence of collaborative co-authoring: active comments, @mentions, and suggestions.
Named milestone versions saved in Version History reflecting editorial stages.
Embedding of smart chips for dates, team assignees, and document references.

deliverables.title: Google Sheets Team Tracker
deliverables.scenario: Build a collaborative project and task operations tracker in Google Sheets featuring data validation dropdowns, status calculations, and conditional formatting.
requirements: Core columns: Task ID, Task Description, Assignee, Priority, Status, Due Date, and Notes.
Data validation dropdown menus for Status (Not Started, In Progress, Blocked, Complete) and Priority.
Essential formulas: SUM, AVERAGE, COUNTIF for task completion, and conditional formatting for overdue items.
Protected ranges and collaborative filter views configured for concurrent multi-user editing.

deliverables.title: Google Slides Project Presentation
deliverables.scenario: Design a clean, 5- to 7-slide executive briefing deck in Google Slides summarizing project goals, milestones, task statuses, and next steps with visual consistency.
requirements: Consistent slide theme, brand colors, readable typography, and whitespace discipline.
Embedded linked chart or summary table imported from the Google Sheets tracker.
Structured slide layouts (Title, Executive Summary, Milestone Roadmap, Status KPIs, Next Actions).
Export-ready formatting with alternative text and screen-reader accessible reading orders.

deliverables.title: Google Forms Response Workflow
deliverables.scenario: Create an office service request or stakeholder feedback form in Google Forms, capture synthetic submissions, and route records to a dedicated response spreadsheet.
requirements: Logical question architecture with appropriate types (short answer, dropdown, linear scale, date).
Input validation and required fields to guarantee data completeness.
Linked response spreadsheet destination with verified timestamp logging.
Independent permissions audit ensuring Form editors and Sheet viewers are configured correctly.

deliverables.title: Meeting Coordination Package
deliverables.scenario: Assemble a complete meeting management package connecting calendar invitations, Meet session details, Docs agendas, and follow-up communication.
requirements: Calendar meeting plan with timezone-validated schedule and Google Meet video link.
Structured meeting agenda in Google Docs with stated discussion topics and time limits.
Professional Gmail invitation draft with clear purpose, attendee roles, and preparation instructions.
Meeting notes template and post-meeting follow-up email draft with assigned action items.

deliverables.title: Access Permission Matrix
deliverables.scenario: Document an exhaustive permissions audit covering every folder, document, spreadsheet, presentation, and form in the workspace to enforce least-privilege access.
requirements: Inventory of all workspace assets detailing Owner, Intended Audience, and Sharing Mode.
Explicit assignment of Viewer, Commenter, and Editor roles for every stakeholder.
Identification of inherited folder permissions and segregation of restricted confidential files.
Separate verification of Google Forms collaborators vs linked response Sheet collaborators.

deliverables.title: Safe Handover SOP Document
deliverables.scenario: Prepare a professional handover standard operating procedure detailing workspace structure, maintenance rules, privacy guidelines, and ownership transition steps.
requirements: Complete workspace index mapping folder purposes, file dependencies, and update rhythms.
Step-by-step instructions for transferring file ownership and archiving completed projects.
Privacy checklist verifying that no personal PII or unapproved public links remain active.
Version-control protocols and disaster recovery instructions using Google Drive trash and revision history.

breakdown.area: Drive organization, file ownership and security
Forms, response handling and team coordination
Gemini verification and final integrated capstone

assessment_model.completionRule: Students must submit the complete integrated Collaborative Digital Office Workspace comprising all eight components. A visually polished workspace that fails permission auditing, exposes public links, or fails to verify linked Forms/Sheets security will not receive passing evaluation.

faq.question: What is Google Workspace — Cloud Productivity & Collaboration?
faq.answer: It is a practical course teaching connected Google applications for communication, documents, meetings, reporting and teamwork.

faq.question: How long is the course?
faq.answer: Five weeks with 40 learning hours.

faq.question: What is the course fee?
faq.answer: ₹5,900, subject to verified Nova Skills pricing and tax policy.

faq.question: Is it suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. Basic computer and internet knowledge are sufficient.

faq.question: Which Google applications are covered?
faq.answer: Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Calendar, Meet and Forms.

faq.question: What is the difference between a personal Google account and Google Workspace?
faq.answer: Personal accounts provide access to many Google productivity tools. Paid Workspace editions add organization-oriented controls and features depending on the plan.

faq.question: Must I purchase Google Workspace?
faq.answer: Not for every core collaboration exercise. Certain business and AI features require eligible paid plans.

faq.question: Will I learn Google Drive?
faq.answer: Yes, including folder organization, file sharing, ownership and version history.

faq.question: What are Viewer, Commenter and Editor permissions?
faq.answer: They are access roles that determine how collaborators can use or modify shared files.

faq.question: Can folder permissions affect files inside them?
faq.answer: Yes. Drive supports inherited permissions, so folder-level sharing must be reviewed.

faq.question: Will I learn Gmail productivity?
faq.answer: Yes, including professional emails, labels, filters and search.

faq.question: Will I learn Calendar scheduling?
faq.answer: Yes, including invitations, recurring meetings, meeting details and follow-ups.

faq.question: Will I learn Google Meet?
faq.answer: Yes, including meeting participation and basic coordination.

faq.question: Is Meet recording free for everyone?
faq.answer: No. Recording depends on eligible account plans and permissions.

faq.question: Will I learn Google Docs collaboration?
faq.answer: Yes, including comments, suggestions and version history.

faq.question: Will I learn Google Sheets?
faq.answer: Yes, for basic formulas, team trackers and reporting.

faq.question: Will I learn Google Slides?
faq.answer: Yes, for collaborative business presentations.

faq.question: Is this a complete Google Sheets or presentation design specialization?
faq.answer: No. The course focuses on practical cloud-office operations.

faq.question: Will I learn Google Forms?
faq.answer: Yes, including form creation, response collection and linking responses to Sheets.

faq.question: Do Forms and linked Sheets have the same permissions?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Their permissions may need to be reviewed separately.

faq.question: Will I learn Google Tasks?
faq.answer: Yes, as a supporting tool for basic task coordination.

faq.question: Will I learn Gemini?
faq.answer: Yes, through responsible AI assistance and eligible feature demonstrations.

faq.question: Is Gemini included in every free Google account?
faq.answer: No. Workspace-integrated Gemini capabilities depend on eligible plans and feature requirements.

faq.question: Can Gemini generate presentations in Google Slides?
faq.answer: Eligible plans support certain Gemini presentation-generation capabilities, subject to current availability and limits.

faq.question: Will I learn Apps Script?
faq.answer: Only introductory awareness or optional demonstrations. Complex scripting is excluded.

faq.question: Is a business email domain required?
faq.answer: No. The core training can use accessible tools and authorized practice accounts.

faq.question: Will I learn Workspace Admin Console?
faq.answer: No. Enterprise domain administration is outside this certification.

faq.question: What will I build for the portfolio?
faq.answer: A collaborative office workspace containing documents, a tracker, a presentation, a Forms workflow, meeting coordination and a permissions audit.

faq.question: Will the course use real company information?
faq.answer: No real confidential data is required. Synthetic or authorized practice information can be used.

faq.question: Who should enroll?
faq.answer: Office staff, remote workers, freelancers, administrators, students and entrepreneurs who need practical cloud collaboration skills.
